correctness.rationale: For k=1,2,3 the radius-two clique complex of P_k times any finite tree reduces by explicit closed-neighborhood dominated-vertex leaf removal, verified for each possible path coordinate. The full graph metric projects all C_n times T faces to one of n three-column strips for n>=7; every nonempty strip intersection is a contractible width-one or width-two tree strip. The nerve is the triangulated square C_n and collapses via unique skip-edge free triangles to C_n, proving X_2 is integrally S^1. At radius one the graph is triangle-free. The product square 2-cells have an injective cellular boundary with primitive image because |C_n| times |T| is homotopy S^1; every boundary fills in a radius-two tetrahedron. Projection onto C_n and a fixed-tree-vertex section establish the surviving primitive integral generator, hence the exact kernel. The n=6 one-vertex tree yields octahedral S^2. Twenty independent exact finite face/chain calculations and a byte-identical replay corroborate, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Cylindrical shortest-path graph products of arbitrarily branched finite trees are a natural unbounded topological family. The theorem strengthens the known width-two circular ladder and complete-clique-fiber results by proving a sharp universal radius-two homotopy classification for branching fibers and by giving an exact primitive integral persistence kernel with geometrically specified square generators. Such a map-level lattice description is mathematically useful for comparing geometric versus spurious graph-product cycles, beyond a textbook renaming or isolated finite census.
